evidence.note: The second Yang Chun is the same subject as the first; source Chun appears three times. Preserve Xing separately.

context.zh: 邢剛直循理，將士嚴憚之，時臥病，聞春亂，流涕不自禁。
context.en: Xing was a man of stern integrity whom officers and men alike feared. He was bedridden when he heard of Yang Chun's revolt and wept uncontrollably.
context.literal: Xing was upright and followed reason; officers and soldiers stood in awe of him. He lay ill at the time; hearing of Chun's mutiny, he wept uncontrollably.

context.zh: 春遣人舁致之，邢指春大罵，春慚恧無言。
context.en: Yang Chun had him carried in. Xing pointed at him and cursed him to his face. Yang Chun stood silent with shame.
context.literal: Chun sent men to carry him there; Xing pointed at Chun and reviled him loudly; Chun was ashamed and speechless.

context.zh: 春欲殺荊山家，邢力勸止之，且令給道路費送之出城，邢尋病卒。
context.en: Yang Chun wanted to slaughter Jingshan's family. Xing talked him out of it and had travel money provided to send them out of the city. Xing soon died of his illness.
context.literal: Chun wished to kill Jingshan's family; Xing strongly urged him to stop and also ordered travel expenses given to send them out of the city; Xing soon died of illness.

evidence.note: Jin envoys, fall of Jin, and Jin gaining/losing the realm are polity references.

context.zh: 於是，因世英以用安終不赴援，乃還朝，至宿州西，遇大兵，不屈而死，事聞，贈汝州防禦使。
context.en: Because Yong'an never marched to the relief, Yin Shiying returned to court. West of Suzhou he met Mongol troops and died rather than submit. When the report reached the capital he was posthumously made defender of Ruzhou.
context.literal: Thereupon, because Yong'an in the end did not march to the relief, Yin Shiying returned to court; west of Suzhou he encountered the great army and died without yielding; when the matter was reported he was posthumously made defender of Ruzhou.

context.zh: 既而用安軍食不給，乞糧于宋，宋陽許之，即改從宋衣冠，而私與朝使相親。
context.en: Before long Yong'an's army ran out of food. He begged grain from the Song, who pretended to agree. He adopted Song dress but kept up private contact with Jin envoys.
context.literal: Before long Yong'an's army lacked food; he begged grain from the Song; the Song pretended to agree, and he immediately adopted Song dress, yet privately kept close ties with Jin envoys.

context.zh: 尋益乏食，軍民多亡去，乃命蕭均以嚴刑禁亡者，血流滿道。
context.en: Food grew still scarcer and soldiers and civilians fled in droves. He ordered Xiao Jun to enforce desertion with brutal punishments until blood ran in the streets.
context.literal: Soon food grew still scarcer; soldiers and civilians fled in great numbers; he then ordered Xiao Jun to use harsh punishments to forbid desertion, and blood flowed full in the streets.

evidence.note: Jin envoys, fall of Jin, and Jin gaining/losing the realm are polity references.

context.zh: 而青、徐、淮海之郊民心一搖，歲遇饑饉，盜賊蜂起，相為長雄，又自屠滅，害及無辜，十餘年糜沸未息。
context.en: Yet in Qing, Xu, and the Huai-Hai borderlands popular loyalty wavered. Famine followed famine. Bandits rose in swarms, made one another chieftains, and slaughtered one another. Innocents suffered. For more than ten years the region seethed without rest.
context.literal: Yet in the borderlands of Qing, Xu, and the Huai-Hai the people's hearts were shaken at once; year after year famine came; bandits rose like bees; they made one another chieftains and then slaughtered one another; harm reached the innocent; for more than ten years turmoil boiled without ceasing.

context.zh: 宣宗不思靖難，複為伐宋之舉，迄金之亡，其禍尤甚。
context.en: Emperor Xuanzong did not seek to quell the disorders but launched another campaign against the Song. Down to the fall of Jin the calamity only grew worse.
context.literal: Emperor Xuanzong did not think of quelling the disorders but again undertook an expedition against the Song; down to the Jin's fall the calamity was still greater.

context.zh: 簡書所載國用安、時青等遺事，至今仁人君子讀之猶蹙頞終日。
context.en: The surviving accounts of Guo Yong'an, Shi Qing, and men like them still make humane readers knit their brows for a whole day.
context.literal: The surviving accounts of Guo Yong'an, Shi Qing, and the like recorded in the annals still make humane gentlemen knit their brows for a whole day when they read them.

evidence.note: Jin envoys, fall of Jin, and Jin gaining/losing the realm are polity references.

context.zh: 兵，兇器也。
context.en: Arms are instruments of ill omen.
context.literal: Arms are an instrument of ill omen.

context.zh: 金以兵得國，亦以兵失國，可不慎哉，可不慎哉！
context.en: Jin won the realm through arms and lost it through arms. How can one not be cautious—how can one not be cautious!
context.literal: Jin gained the realm through arms and also lost the realm through arms—how can one not be cautious, how can one not be cautious!

evidence.note: Read s0232-s0256: the commander Shi Quan refuses Eke, delays the army, escapes by boat, and is condemned. This is not Li Quan.

context.zh: 眾惑之，訛可及諸將佐勸之不聽，軍留三日。
context.en: The troops were perplexed. Eke and the other generals urged him to move on, but he refused, and the army stayed three days.
context.literal: The troops were perplexed; Eke and the generals and staff urged him but he would not listen, and the army remained three days.

context.zh: 訛可謂全曰：「今淮水淺狹，可以速濟。
context.en: Eke said to Quan: "The Huai is shallow and narrow now. We can cross quickly.
context.literal: Eke said to Quan: "The Huai is now shallow and narrow and can be crossed quickly.

context.zh: 時方暑雨，若值暴漲，宋乘其後，將不得完歸矣。」
context.en: It is the season of summer rains. If a sudden flood comes and the Song strike from behind, we will not get the army home intact."
context.literal: It is the season of summer rains; if a sudden flood comes and the Song strike from behind, the army will not be able to return intact."

evidence.note: Read s0232-s0256: the commander Shi Quan refuses Eke, delays the army, escapes by boat, and is condemned. This is not Li Quan.

context.zh: 橋壞，全以輕舟先濟，士卒皆覆沒。
context.en: The bridge collapsed. Quan escaped in a light boat while the soldiers were drowned.
context.literal: The bridge broke; Quan crossed first in a light boat and the soldiers were all drowned.

context.zh: 宣宗乃下詔誅之，遣官招集潰軍，詔曰：「大軍渡淮，每立功效。
context.en: Emperor Xuanzong issued an edict condemning Quan and sent officials to gather the scattered troops. The edict read: "The great army crossed the Huai and repeatedly achieved merit.
context.literal: Emperor Xuanzong then issued an edict condemning him and sent officials to gather the scattered troops; the edict said: "The great army crossed the Huai and repeatedly achieved merit.

context.zh: 諸將謬誤，部曲散亡，流離憂苦，朕甚閔焉。
context.en: The generals erred. Units scattered and men wander in distress. We are deeply grieved.
context.literal: The generals erred, the units scattered and perished, and the men wander in distress—I am deeply grieved.

evidence.note: Local record p128 begins this continuous Shi Quan episode; leave cross-chunk duplicate identity resolution separate.

context.zh: 興定五年正月二十五日夜，青襲破泗州西城，提控王祿遇害。
context.en: On the night of the twenty-fifth of the first month of Xingding 5, Qing stormed and took Sizhou's western city. Commander Wang Lu was killed.
context.literal: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the first month of the fifth year of Xingding, Qing raided and broke Sizhou's western city; commander Wang Lu was killed.

context.zh: 是時，時全為同簽樞密院事，朝廷不知青襲破西城，止稱宋人而已。
context.en: Shi Quan was then co-signatory of the Privy Council. The court did not know Qing had taken the western city and reported only that Song troops were responsible.
context.literal: At that time Shi Quan was co-signatory of the Privy Council; the court did not know Qing had raided and broken the western city and spoke only of Song men.

context.zh: 詔全往督泗州兵取西城。
context.en: An edict ordered Quan to supervise the Sizhou garrison in retaking the western city.
context.literal: An edict ordered Quan to go and supervise Sizhou troops in retaking the western city.
